content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves, leading to overcorrection in subsequent days — model should cap upward momentum after >+10% spike.
- Mean reversion is overestimated — model too aggressively pulls prices back to historical mean after spikes, ignoring sustained momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model should not assume volatility is low — instead, treat as “high uncertainty” and widen forecast range or reduce confidence.
- In multi-day horizon (30d), model tends to underestimate late-period price action — especially after mid-period spikes — suggesting need to adjust for tail risk or delayed reaction.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a flat period, model should not reset to prior mean — instead, apply a “trend continuation” bias for 3-5 days.
- When sentiment history is all 0.00, model should not ignore recent price momentum — instead, use 3-5 day moving average as baseline for correction.
